skill.author: inference-sh-9

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are markdown fences, inline code formatting, or documentation links, not executable code. The real issues are unpinned npx install instructions, a remote shadcn registry URL, and a remotely hosted image asset.

remediation.issue: Unpinned shadcn install command uses npx shadcn@latest with a remote registry URL.
remediation.suggestion: Pin the shadcn CLI version, document the source domain, and provide checksum or commit-based verification for the registry content.

remediation.issue: Related skill examples use npx skills add with remote skill references.
remediation.suggestion: Pin package and skill versions in examples, and state that users should review remote skill contents before installing them.

remediation.issue: The README embeds a remote image from cloud.inference.sh.
remediation.suggestion: Bundle the image locally or state that rendering the documentation may request a remote asset from the provider domain.

content.user_title: Add Tool Lifecycle UI to Agent Apps
content.value_statement: Agent applications need clear tool status, approval, and result displays. This skill provides React and Next.js component guidance for those workflows.
actual_capabilities: Shows how to install tool UI components from the ui.inference.sh shadcn registry.
Documents component states for pending, running, approval, success, and error flows.
Provides examples for ToolCall, ToolResult, and ToolApproval components.
Shows a full Agent component integration with approval-required tools.
Lists icon mappings for common tool name patterns.
limitations: The skill is documentation only and does not include component source files.
Examples assume a React or Next.js project with compatible shadcn setup.
Remote install commands depend on the availability of ui.inference.sh services.
Approval callbacks must be implemented by the host application.

use_cases.title: Agent Tool Status Panels
use_cases.description: Display pending, running, success, and error states for agent tool calls in a React interface.

use_cases.title: Human Approval Workflows
use_cases.description: Add approve and deny controls before sensitive tools execute in an agent application.

use_cases.title: Tool Result Presentation
use_cases.description: Render structured tool outputs in a consistent interface for operators and end users.

prompt_templates.title: Install the Components
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner setup in an existing app
prompt_templates.prompt: Add the tools UI components to my React or Next.js project. Explain any install steps before changing files.

prompt_templates.title: Render Tool States
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the tool UI components to show pending, running, success, and error states for my agent tool calls.

prompt_templates.title: Add Approval Controls
prompt_templates.prompt: Build a tool approval view that shows tool arguments and calls my approve or deny handlers.

prompt_templates.title: Integrate with an Agent
prompt_templates.prompt: Connect the Agent component to my tool list and show approval gates only for tools marked as sensitive.

output_examples.input: A user asks to show a web search tool while it is running.
output_examples.output: A compact tool card appears with a search icon, the tool name, visible arguments, and a running status indicator.

output_examples.input: A user asks to add approval before sending an email tool call.
output_examples.output: The interface shows the email tool name, recipient and subject details, plus approve and deny actions.

output_examples.input: A user asks to display successful tool results in the agent transcript.
output_examples.output: The result area shows the completed tool name, success status, and a readable summary of returned data.

best_practices: Review remote registry content before running install commands in production projects.
Require approval for tools that send messages, write files, delete data, or call paid services.
Keep tool arguments visible enough for users to make informed approval decisions.
anti_patterns: Do not hide tool arguments when asking users to approve sensitive actions.
Do not treat UI approval as a replacement for server-side authorization checks.
Do not install remote component registries without reviewing their contents and version sources.

faq.question: What does this skill help build?
faq.answer: It helps build React and Next.js interfaces for agent tool calls, approvals, statuses, and results.

faq.question: Does it include executable component code?
faq.answer: No. The skill provides documentation and install guidance for components hosted by ui.inference.sh.

faq.question: Which tools can use this skill?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Does it handle approval logic for me?
faq.answer: It shows UI patterns for approval flows. Your application must implement the approve and deny behavior.

faq.question: Can I use it without Next.js?
faq.answer: The examples target React and Next.js projects. Other React setups may need path and build adjustments.

faq.question: What should I review before installation?
faq.answer: Review the remote registry content, package versions, and any related skills before running npx commands.
